paper_title: Partial and Exact Recovery of a Random Hypergraph from its Graph Projection
authors: Guy Bresler, Chenghao Guo, Yury Polyanskiy, Andrew Yao
statement: 2. A specific instance of the above non-uniform hyperedge problem arises in the context of random intersection graphs (RIG). Each node i ∈ [n] is associated with an independent random subsets Si of [m] such that j ∈ [m] is an element of Si independently with probability p. The RIG includes edge {u, v} if and only if Su and Sv are not disjoint. For j ∈ [m], define Cj to be the set of i ∈ [n] such that j ∈ Si , and note that the graph has a clique on each Cj . When can one recover the sets Cj , given the graph? Brennan et al. (2020) finds a phase transition for the total variation convergence of an RIG to Erdös-Rényi. We expect a phase transition to occur for the feasibility of recovering the cliques Cj .
context: 1. A potential future direction is to study the same recovery questions but for non-uniform hypergraphs, i.e., when the hyperedges have differing sizes.
